proof_summary: Letting \(d=D(n)\), the congruence \(n\equiv d\pmod 9\) gives \(\gcd(9,d)\mid n\), so one can choose \(m\) with \(d\mid n+9m\); periodicity of powers of \(10\) modulo \(d\) then lets one place \(n-m\) digits \(1\) in one congruence class of positions and \(m\) in positions shifted by one, producing a multiple \(k_0\) of \(d\) with digit sum exactly \(n\). Multiplying \(k_0\) by a sufficiently large power of \(10\) preserves these properties while making it larger than \(n\), hence it is a distinct partner since \(D(n)\mid k\) and \(D(k)=n\mid n\).
